title: Plant map
description: Mapping of OPC UA nodes and control values for a plant. This mapping is DATA that the owner must confirm against the real control system; no vendor semantics are assumed, and the schema does not know what any raw value means.

version.description: Version of this plant map schema layout.

endpoint.description: OPC UA endpoint URL, must start with "opc.tcp://".

node.description: OPC UA NodeId text of the node that receives the gateway heartbeat counter.

ack_node.description: Optional OPC UA NodeId text of the node the control system writes when it sees the heartbeat.

targets.description: Mapping from target tag name to its node and control configuration.

setpoint_node.description: OPC UA NodeId text of the setpoint node, e.g. "ns=2;s=Plant.FIC101.SP" or "nsu=urn:x;s=Plant.FIC101.SP". Written by the gateway; units are the engineering units of the tag.

readback_node.description: OPC UA NodeId text of the read-back value, in the engineering units of the tag.

mode_node.description: OPC UA NodeId text of the loop mode node. Raw value is reverse-mapped through mode_values.

source_node.description: OPC UA NodeId text of the node that says who owns the setpoint. May be the same node as mode_node.

remote_value.description: Raw value of source_node meaning the setpoint is owned by remote (gateway) control.

local_value.description: Raw value of source_node meaning the setpoint is owned by local (operator) control.

release_value.description: Raw value written to source_node to hand the setpoint back to local control.

mode_values.description: Mapping from loop mode name to the raw integer value of mode_node.

take_remote.description: Optional. Raw write that puts the setpoint source into remote control. Without it, write() only touches the setpoint node and the control system stays in local setpoint source.

node.description: OPC UA NodeId text of the node that receives the take value. Defaults to source_node.

value.description: Raw value written to take the setpoint source to remote.

before_setpoint.description: Write the take before the setpoint (true) or after it (false).
